title: Missed bus from Columbia and string of road accidents
summary: He tells of chasing a Greyhound eight miles, a bus with bad tires, and several car wrecks, including one into a barbershop.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You were on Greyhound? Yeah, we was on Greyhound. In those days I guess they weren't so modern anyway. No they weren't so modern.

So all the other people, they wanted to get on ahead of us, so the bus driver told them and said no, so let these musicians get on first because if it don't be for him, none of us would have got home, see, we'd have turned over, you know, off the highway. So we got in the bus and sit down and put our instruments up and come on into town. But I can tell when them cars go to swing, you see, that's it, turn over right now. But I done been in a gang of them on the road. But just luck enough I didn't get quite too bad. I've been in six racks. Really? That's right. One night we was coming from Vachery, Louisiana, on that old river road, and I told the fellow, I said, listen, I said, you're driving on the wrong side of the highway. I said, keep to your right. All ain't nothing coming. Just then there come a truck. Shooting around the curb and I grabbed the wheel and we took the ditch. Turned over and the drum player he broke his ankle. Who was that? We called him Lagre Mas, I forget this little fellow, he was a little Creole fellow that lived downtown. And he broke his ankle. All of us could have got killed. Didn't get a scratch on him. But we lucky. Turned over the whole truck. I mean turned over, running the ditch. Well I had to do that because he'd had a head on. Oh yeah, he'd get killed. So I always stay awake when I'm driving. Or whoever's driving I always watch him, you know, because he's staying up. I'd have been in all kind of wrecks. After all, I was a kid. I'd have been in all kind of wrecks. After all those wrecks I don't blame you. I played music too. I've seen us, we come from Picayune, I used to play at the end of Picayune Jones' Jewry Store. And we was coming home, it was raining. I lived down here on Cleveland Street. And I told the fellow, I said, now look, I said, watch these corners. He said, okay. We got to the corner here, a fellow slid right into us, boom, and hit us and we run up in the barbershop. Didn't get no scratch on me again. I said, must be a...
You ran your car up into the barbershop? Yes, indeed.
Through the window? It hit us right up in the door.
I said, Lord, I'm a kid. There it is again. Lucky again.
Well, out of all that we come out, God's good, we. Yeah? Ain't got broke up yet.
